title: Benchmark for Safety in Tool-Augmented Retrieval (RAG) Pipelines
original_idea: Construct 120 RAG scenarios where retrieved context contains harmful content. Measure whether the model propagates, qualifies, or refuses the harmful retrieved content across three models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: RAG is one of the most widely deployed architectures. Safety evaluations ignoring retrieved context leave a major attack surface uncharacterized. Extremely practically relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Setting up RAG pipelines with LangChain/LlamaIndex is documented. Creating harmful retrieved contexts and evaluating model responses is moderately complex. Accessible with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 120 scenarios, three models, RAG pipeline setup. Designing harmful retrieved contexts and classification criteria adds scope. Moderate for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: 'RAG LLMs are Not Safer: A Safety Analysis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models' (NAACL 2025) directly demonstrates that RAG can make models less safe and change their safety profile, even with safe documents. 'Benchmarking Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation' (arXiv:2505.18543, 2025) provides a unified benchmark framework for RAG poisoning attacks. PoisonedRAG (arXiv:2402.07867, 2024) achieved 97% attack success rate on NQ. 'Machine Against the RAG' (USENIX Security 2025) and 'Practical Poisoning Attacks against RAG' (arXiv:2504.03957, 2025) further characterize the attack surface. The proposed 120 scenarios measuring propagation vs. qualification vs. refusal across three models closely overlaps with this body of work, particularly the NAACL 2025 paper which directly studies how models handle harmful retrieved content.
